clue.text: Musical work, one in scales, still including chanting in the middle

parts.note: a trout is a fish, a creature covered in scales

indicators.note: including means the word for still holds the other letters within it

parts.note: still means quiet

indicators.note: in the middle picks out the central pair of letters from the word chanting

explanation.surface: A description of a piece of music: someone practising scales while chanting goes on in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in scales' tempts a musician practising; it is a fish. 'Including' wraps the word for still around the central pair of chanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert's Trout Quintet is a well-known chamber composition, so it is an example of a musical work.

clue.text: Provisional speed on approximately 28 per cent of railway lines

parts.note: tempo is the speed at which music is played

indicators.note: two of the seven letters of railway is about 28 per cent, so take its opening pair of letters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines of track

explanation.surface: A temporary speed limit on a stretch of railway track, given with mock statistical precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approximately 28 per cent of' railway is RA, two letters of seven; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an arrangement meant to last only for a while until replaced: a synonym.

clue.text: Who, originally on Antarctic, tendered extreme sacrifice?

definitions.text: Who, originally on Antarctic, tendered extreme sacrifice?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A quiz question about the polar explorer who gave his life on Scott's expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the last five words spell the name, and the whole clue also describes the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Lawrence Oates walked out into a blizzard on Scott's Antarctic expedition to save his companions, a famous self-sacrifice.

clue.text: Actual commotion successively cut short in city

indicators.note: each of the two words in turn loses its final letter

parts.note: actual means true
a row is a noisy commotion

explanation.surface: A real disturbance repeatedly interrupted somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Successively cut short' removes the last letter of TRUE and then of ROW. Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the only city in the county of Cornwall, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Given little employment, no-hoper wanting best friend gets exploited

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following word is removed

parts.note: an underdog is the one nobody expects to win
the dog is called man's best friend
exploited means used

explanation.surface: A neglected worker, a born loser without a pal, is taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' strips DOG, 'man's best friend', from UNDERDOG, leaving UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom put to work has been employed less than it could be: a paraphrase.

clue.text: Even nerds will get twitchy in terminals

indicators.note: twitchy suggests jerky, jumbled movement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Even computer nerds grow fidgety sitting at their terminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminals' looks like computer screens for nerds; here it means endings of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve endings are the terminal points of nerve fibres, so they are terminals in the body.

clue.text: Soaring cheers honour old enemy vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the letters go upwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Cheers rise as an honour is given for sinking an enemy ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaring' reverses TA OBE in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: German fast torpedo boats in the Second World War were called E-boats by the Allies: an enemy craft.

clue.text: Shrink from circus performer

definitions.meaning: slang for a psychiatrist; this phrase is jokey British slang for one
taken literally, a stunt rider on a unicycle or bike

explanation.surface: A circus act retreats in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as slang it is a psychiatrist (a shrink); read literally it is a rider doing stunts in the ring.

clue.text: Brief watch perhaps retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a watch is an example of a timer

explanation.surface: A short timepiece of some sort is pulled back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the watch; it is the noun, a set of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief and a remit are both the scope of a task someone is given: synonyms.

clue.text: Court and English criminal gloss over this?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court and an English criminal cover up wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss over' seems to mean hush up; here gloss is shiny paint applied on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss paint is applied over a base coat of primer-like paint, so this layer lies under it.

clue.text: With South annexed, first learnt about those wishing to change sides?

indicators.note: annexed means taken in, so the letter is added inside
about means around or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Political defectors learn first about switching allegiance once the South is annexed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change sides' suggests turncoats; in football it is players leaving their club. 'About' rearranges first learnt; 'annexed' takes S in.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's transfer list names footballers available to move to another team, often at their own request.

clue.text: Whizz-round makes route mostly confused

parts.note: to cook something is to make it, as in cooking up a scheme

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A rushed trip produces a route that is largely muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims route to ROUT, and 'confused' rearranges that. Thomas Cook was a British travel firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid, superficial guided trip around sights is called this, after the Thomas Cook travel company's tours.

clue.text: Perhaps wide on the right, but not the ends

indicators.note: means the first and last letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: dextral means right-handed or on the right side

explanation.surface: A winger playing wide on the right, but not out at the ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wide' sounds like a footballer's position; in cricket a wide is a ball out of the batter's reach, scored as a run not off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wide is one kind of run conceded without the bat, so it is an example of this.

clue.text: Daily and regularly, oilman is providing specific stock

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of oilman

explanation.surface: A cleaner and an oil worker turn up regularly, providing a particular stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shares for an oilman; it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Charolais is a French breed of beef cattle, so it is a particular kind of livestock.

clue.text: Novel in transit

definitions.meaning: a book by Jack Kerouac, the Beat classic

explanation.surface: A book about travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Jack Kerouac's famous 1957 book, and the phrase also means travelling between places.

clue.text: Overbearing musical backing engulfing ship (QE2)

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing other letters inside
backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
SS stands for steamship
Queen Elizabeth II is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A domineering musical tie-in sponsored by a cruise liner, the QE2.
explanation.walkthrough: 'QE2' looks like the liner; it is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina. 'Backing' turns the show's name round to ATIVE, and 'engulfing' takes the ship and the Queen inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forcefully self-assured, pushing their views, is both overbearing and this: near-synonyms.

clue.text: Animals needing intelligence to grasp time

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold the other letter inside

parts.note: intelligence can mean information, news

explanation.surface: Creatures needing brains to understand time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' looks like brainpower; it is information.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts are small amphibians, so they are examples of animals.

clue.text: Fry a little morsel, adding shelled peas separately

indicators.note: separately means the two pea letters do not stay together: the second one goes into the other piece

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters are removed, leaving the middle

parts.note: a bit is a small morsel

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: fry a small portion and add shelled peas on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' is the definition, not a cooking verb: young fish. 'Separately' means the two pea letters part company, one after the first word and one inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry are young fish, and whitebait are the tiny fry of herring and sprats.

clue.text: Shout by one's coach in vault

parts.note: to shout is to cry out
a PT, a personal trainer, is someone's coach

explanation.surface: A cry from a gym instructor as an athlete vaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests gymnastics with a coach; it is an underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vaulted chamber beneath a church: a synonym.

clue.text: Teams cancel, getting unexpected flak

parts.note: teams are sides
to wipe something is to erase or cancel it

explanation.surface: Teams call off a fixture and are criticised out of the blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing critical remark made in the course of something else is an incidental attack: idiom.

clue.text: Brief publication that is circulating an idea

indicators.note: circulating means going round the other letters

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A short magazine putting an idea into circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a mental picture or concept of something, close to an idea.

clue.text: English novelist with husband following specific religion

indicators.note: following means the letter comes after

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists

explanation.surface: An English writer and her husband following a particular faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Protestant Anabaptist sect, a particular faith group, known for plain living.

clue.text: Ex US president on call — lines sound familiar

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the following piece comes after

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
Abe is Abraham Lincoln
L is short for line, so two make lines

explanation.surface: A former president on the phone, whose lines seem well known.
explanation.definitionFit: When something rings a bell it stirs a memory, seeming familiar: an idiom.

clue.text: Given more of these, you'll want more

definitions.text: Given more of these, you'll want more

parts.words: Given more of these, you'll want more
parts.note: a paradox: having more requirements means wanting more things

explanation.surface: A greedy maxim: the more you get, the more you want.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are what someone lacks, so more of them means more wants, a near-synonym of wants.

clue.text: Port, a small volume, rather acidic to begin with

parts.note: cc is cubic centimetre, a small volume

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A port wine in a small measure tastes rather sour at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the drink; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana and a seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Fossil of worm, one with well-worn exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the word is on the outside of the other letters

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, well-worn
a lob or lobworm is a lugworm used as bait
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fossilised worm with a battered outer surface.
explanation.walkthrough: LOB, a lugworm, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites were ancient marine arthropods now known only from fossil remains: an example.

clue.text: Credit fool with immense stupidity

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Crediting a fool with extraordinary stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass describes behaviour that is grossly insensitive and dense: a synonym phrase.

clue.text: There's no turning back, having hesitated (sic) disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously suggests wreckage, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Having hesitated, someone finds they cannot go back, with sic marking a quoted slip.
explanation.walkthrough: '(sic)' looks like an editor's aside; its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's saying at the Rubicon means a decision has been made irrevocably: idiom.
